by FVanon

I don't really know how to prove it as I don't have pics, but this is what I saw: yoga, drum circles, human microphone, people doing that hippie clap with the wiggly fingers, and some guy with a reddit sign that said "we are the 99%". Just some things that stick out in memory.

Anyway, what I witnessed was a completely inane clusterfuck that should have never existed. From the get go, Occupy Wall Street never happened. At all. Because the cops said no. They moved the hippies to a small park on Broadway and Cedar, away from the financial district, so the only thing that got occupied was that small park. The embarrassment that ensued was soul crushing. Nobody had a plan. And I mean nobody at all. There was no focus, no demand, and no sense whatsoever. There was a whole pro- Ron Paul group. There was another anti- Ron Paul crowd. There were people trying (with some success) to piggyback a campaign for some guy on death row in Georgia. There were some 9/11 truthers and other crazies, and there were people who were heatedly arguing with them. A whole lot of people were accusing a whole lot of other people of being with the police. It was a smelly, paranoid, clusterfuck. In essence, there was no unifying or overarching goal, strategy, or method to speak of.

The blogs horribly over reported this thing too, soiling the credibility of these people even further. The numbers were in the mid-hundreds at the beginning (~4pm saturday) and when I saw them again later at night (~11PM), they dwindled to maybe 70-90, though some "pledged to come back" in the morning.

I've made my personal position on this thing rather clear: I find it silly, embarrassing, and belittling of the idea of activism.

I'll answer any questions you have about what I saw or what I think of it.
